biography: Phil McGarty, a name now synonymous with raw speed and unapologetic flair, hails from the unassuming town of Market Rasen in Lincolnshire. His journey began not on the track, but in the muddy fields surrounding his family's farm, tearing around on a battered quad bike. That early recklessness, honed by countless hours of near misses, translated surprisingly well to four wheels. A chance encounter with a local Ginetta racer, impressed by Phil's fearless driving on a makeshift karting track at a village fete, led to an unexpected sponsorship. McGarty’s first season was a baptism by fire, full of spins and the occasional dented barrier, but his natural talent was undeniable. He quickly rose through the Ginetta ranks, his aggressive style both thrilling and divisive. Now, at 26, McGarty is at the peak of his powers, a force to be reckoned with in the Ginetta GT Championship, aiming for the top prize.
drivingStyle: McCarty's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He's an aggressive late-braker, unafraid to throw the car into corners and wrestle it back into line. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers to extract every last ounce of performance from the tires in the initial stages of a race, often leaving him vulnerable in the closing laps. Under pressure, McGarty tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to errors, but also to spectacular overtakes. He lives for the thrill of the chase, relishing wheel-to-wheel combat.

rivalries.reason: Rossi, a calculated and precise driver, represents everything McGarty isn't. Their contrasting styles often clash on track, leading to tense battles and the occasional post-race barb.

Eldridge is a veteran Ginetta racer known for his meticulous preparation and tactical racing. McGarty sees Eldridge as an 'old man' blocking his way to the top, and has been vocal about Eldridge's perceived 'lack of excitement.'

Sanderson and McGarty were teammates for one season, but their relationship soured after a controversial incident where Sanderson allegedly blocked McGarty during qualifying, costing him a potential pole position.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of red socks, no matter how smelly they get.
Has to listen to a specific heavy metal song ('Ace of Spades' by Motorhead) exactly three times before every race.
Refuses to sign autographs with a black pen, claiming it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Ginetta GT Supercup at Brands Hatch, overtaking two cars on the final lap with a daring move around the outside of Paddock Hill Bend.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 Ginetta GT Championship finale at Donington Park, costing him the championship.
